arxiv-2012-08901.title: Particle spectra from dark matter annihilation: physics modeling and QCD uncertainties
arxiv-2012-08901.creator: Peter Skands
arxiv-2012-08901.description: Abstract In this talk, we discuss the physics modelling of particle spectra arising from dark matter (DM) annihilation or decay. In the context of the indirect searches of DM, the final state products will, in general, undergo a set of complicated processes such as resonance decays, QED/QCD radiation, hadronisation and hadron decays.

arxiv-2101-01495.title: LSSD: a Controlled Large JPEG Image Database for Deep-Learning-based Steganalysis “into the Wild”
arxiv-2101-01495.creator: Hugo Ruiz, Mehdi Yedroudj, Marc Chaumont, Frédéric Comby, Gérard Subsol
arxiv-2101-01495.description: Abstract For many years, the image databases used in steganalysis have been relatively small, i.e. about ten thousand images. This limits the diversity of images and thus prevents large-scale analysis of steganalysis algorithms. In this paper, we describe a large JPEG database composed of 2 million colour and grey-scale images.

arxiv-2107-04164.title: Parallel and Multi-Objective Falsification with Scenic and VerifAI
arxiv-2107-04164.creator: Kesav Viswanadha, Edward Kim, Francis Indaheng, Daniel J. Fremont, Sanjit A. Seshia
arxiv-2107-04164.description: Abstract Falsification has emerged as an important tool for simulation-based verification of autonomous systems. In this paper, we present extensions to the Scenic scenario specification language and VerifAI toolkit that improve the scalability of sampling-based falsification methods by using parallelism and extend falsification to multi-objective specifications.

arxiv-2108-06169.title: Meteorological factors and non-pharmaceutical interventions explain local differences in the spread of SARS-CoV-2 in Austria
arxiv-2108-06169.creator: Katharina Ledebur 1,2, Michaela Kaleta 1,2, Jiaying Chen 1,2,3, Simon Lindner 1,2, Caspar Matzhold 1,2, Florian Weidle 4, Christoph Wittmann 4, Katharina Habimana 5, Linda Kerschbaumer 5, Sophie Stumpfl 5, Georg Heiler 2,6, Martin Bicher 6,7, Nikolas Popper 6,7,8, Florian Bachner 5, Peter Klimek 1,2
arxiv-2108-06169.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Katharina Ledebur 1,2, Michaela Kaleta 1,2, Jiaying Chen 1,2,3, Simon Lindner 1,2, Caspar Matzhold 1,2, Florian Weidle 4, Christoph Wittmann 4, Katharina Habimana 5, Linda Kerschbaumer 5, Sophie Stumpfl 5, Georg Heiler 2,6, Martin Bicher 6,7, Nikolas Popper 6,7,8, Florian Bachner 5, Peter Klimek 1,2. The drivers behind regional differences of SARS-CoV-2 spread on finer spatio-temporal scales are yet to be fully understood.

arxiv-2301-01475.title: Dynamic Response of Wigner Crystals
arxiv-2301-01475.creator: Lili Zhao, Wenlu Lin, Yoon Jang Chung, Adbhut Gupta, Kirk W. Baldwin, Loren N. Pfeiffer, Yang Liu
arxiv-2301-01475.description: Abstract The Wigner crystal, an ordered array of electrons, is one of the very first proposed many-body phases stabilized by the electron-electron interaction. This electron solid phase has been reported in ultra-clean two-dimensional electron systems at extremely low temperatures, where the Coulomb interaction dominants over the kinetic energy, disorder potential and thermal fluctuation.

arxiv-2301-09798.title: Thermal capillary waves on bounded nanoscale thin films
arxiv-2301-09798.creator: Jingbang Liu, Chengxi Zhao, Duncan A. Lockerby, James E. Sprittles
arxiv-2301-09798.description: Abstract The effect of confining walls on the fluctuation of a nanoscale thin film’s free surface is studied using the stochastic thin-film equations (STFE). Two canonical boundary conditions are employed to reveal the influence of the confinement: (i) an imposed contact angle and (ii) a pinned contact line.

arxiv-2311-10315.title: Interpretable Modeling of Single-cell perturbation Responses to Novel Drugs Using Cycle Consistence Learning
arxiv-2311-10315.creator: Wei Huang, Aichun Zhu, Hui Liu*
arxiv-2311-10315.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wei Huang, Aichun Zhu, Hui Liu*. Phenotype-based screening has attracted much attention for identifying cell-active compounds. Transcriptional and proteomic profiles of cell population or single cells are informative phenotypic measures of cellular responses to perturbations. In this paper, we proposed a deep learning framework based on encoder-decoder architecture that maps the initial cellular states to a latent space, in which we assume the effects of drug perturbation on cellular states follow linear additivity.

arxiv-2312-15096.title: Optimal In-Place Compaction of Sliding Cubes
arxiv-2312-15096.creator: Irina Kostitsyna, Tim Ophelders, Irene Parada, Tom Peters, Willem Sonke, Bettina Speckmann
arxiv-2312-15096.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Irina Kostitsyna, Tim Ophelders, Irene Parada, Tom Peters, Willem Sonke, Bettina Speckmann. The sliding cubes model is a well-established theoretical framework that supports the analysis of reconfiguration algorithms for modular robots consisting of face-connected cubes. The best algorithm currently known for the reconfiguration problem, by Abel and Kominers [arXiv, 2011], uses O ⁡ ( n 3 ) O(n^{3}) moves to transform any n n -cube configuration into any other n n -cube configuration.

arxiv-2404-19414.title: Toward the application of large- N N deconfinement to SU(3) QCD
arxiv-2404-19414.description: Abstract It is generally known for U ⁡ ( N ) \mathrm{U}(N) gauge theory at finite temperature that phase transitions are manifested by taking the large- N N limit. Since the large- N N theory undergoes two thermodynamic phase transitions, a nontrivial intermediate phase can be realized in addition to the phases classified as the conventional confined and deconfined phases.

arxiv-2502-12841.title: Alperin’s bound and normal Sylow subgroups
arxiv-2502-12841.creator: Zhicheng Feng, J. Miquel Martínez, Damiano Rossi
arxiv-2502-12841.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhicheng Feng, J. Miquel Martínez, Damiano Rossi. Let G G be a finite group, p p a prime number and P P a Sylow p p -subgroup of G G . Tiep conjectured that the number of p p -Brauer characters of G G coincides with that of the normaliser 𝐍 G ​ ( P ) {\bf N}_{G}(P) if and only if P P is normal in G G .

arxiv-2503-15427.title: Direct comparison of stochastic-driven nonlinear dynamical systems for combinatorial optimization
arxiv-2503-15427.creator: Junpeng Hou, Amin Barzegar, Helmut G. Katzgraber
arxiv-2503-15427.description: Abstract Combinatorial optimization problems are ubiquitous in industrial applications. However, finding optimal or close-to-optimal solutions can often be extremely hard. Because some of these problems can be mapped to the ground-state search of the Ising model, tremendous effort has been devoted to developing solvers for Ising-type problems over the past decades.

arxiv-2505-20047.title: Grammars of Formal Uncertainty: When to Trust LLMs in Automated Reasoning Tasks
arxiv-2505-20047.creator: Debargha Ganguly, Vikash Singh, Sreehari Sankar, Biyao Zhang, Xuecen Zhang, Srinivasan Iyengar, Xiaotian Han, Amit Sharma, Shivkumar Kalyanaraman, Vipin Chaudhary
arxiv-2505-20047.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) show remarkable promise for democratizing automated reasoning by generating formal specifications. However, a fundamental tension exists: LLMs are probabilistic, while formal verification demands deterministic guarantees. This paper addresses this epistemological gap by comprehensively investigating failure modes and uncertainty quantification (UQ) in LLM-generated formal artifacts.

arxiv-2506-13680.title: Hybrid Meta-learners for Estimating Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
arxiv-2506-13680.creator: Zhongyuan Liang, Lars van der Laan, Ahmed Alaa
arxiv-2506-13680.description: Abstract Estimating conditional average treatment effects (CATE) from observational data involves modeling decisions that differ from supervised learning, particularly concerning how to regularize model complexity. Previous approaches can be grouped into two primary “meta-learner” paradigms that impose distinct inductive biases.

arxiv-2511-01441.title: Galaxy assembly bias in cosmological hydrodynamical simulations – a comparison between SIMBA and Illustris TNG 2026 Galaxy assembly bias in cosmological hydrodynamical simulations – a comparison between SIMBA and Illustris TNG – References
arxiv-2511-01441.creator: Hong-Gang Yang, Marcos Pellejero-Ibá n ~ \mathrm{\tilde{n}} ez, John A. Peacock, Romeel Davé
arxiv-2511-01441.description: Abstract Modelling of large-scale structure is increasingly concerned with galaxy assembly bias (GAB), the dependence of galaxy clustering on quantities other than halo mass. We investigate how baryonic physics affects the strength and redshift evolution of GAB using the largest runs of two state-of-the-art cosmological hydrodynamical simulations: SIMBA and Illustris TNG.

arxiv-2601-08842.title: Resisting Correction: How RLHF Makes Language Models Ignore External Safety Signals in Natural Conversation
arxiv-2601-08842.creator: Felipe Biava Cataneo
arxiv-2601-08842.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Felipe Biava Cataneo. AI safety systems increasingly rely on external monitors to correct model errors, but can language models accept such corrections? We test whether instruction-tuned models can incorporate external confidence signals—a capability critical for modular safety architectures. Using Llama-3.2-3B on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, N=500), we uncover a fundamental design flaw: while base models exhibit high controllability in direct tasks ( ρ = 1.0 \rho=1.0 ), instruction-tuned models demonstrate Context-Dependent Resistance .

arxiv-2601-14173.title: Penalizing Localized Dirichlet Energies in Low Rank Tensor Products
arxiv-2601-14173.creator: Paris A. Karakasis, Nicholas D. Sidiropoulos
arxiv-2601-14173.description: Abstract We study low-rank tensor-product B-spline (TPBS) models for regression tasks and investigate Dirichlet energy as a measure of smoothness. We show that TPBS models admit a closed-form expression for the Dirichlet energy, and reveal scenarios where perfect interpolation is possible with exponentially small Dirichlet energy. This renders global Dirichlet energy-based regularization ineffective.

europmc-pmc3322362.title: Predicting RNA-protein interactions using only sequence information.
europmc-pmc3322362.creator: Muppirala UK, Honavar VG, Dobbs D.
europmc-pmc3322362.description: Background RNA-protein interactions (RPIs) play important roles in a wide variety of cellular processes, ranging from transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression to host defense against pathogens. High throughput experiments to identify RNA-protein int

jewish-encyclopedia-1906-tanhum-b-elieze.creator: Executive Committee of the Editorial Board., Peter Wiernik

pmc-10736333.title: PHENOTYPES OF COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN THE CONTEXT OF COMORBIDITIES
pmc-10736333.creator: Yaguang Zheng, Weiyu Mao, Jing Wang
pmc-10736333.description: While a growing body of evidence has shown that the prevalence of cognitive impairment varies depending on the population, limited research has explored the complex relationships among different cognitive function domains or changes in cognitive functions in the context of comorbidities (e.g., diabetes and stroke).

pmc-11367576.title: Chromium(II)-isophthalate 2D MOF with Redox-Tailorable Gas Adsorption Selectivity
pmc-11367576.creator: Michał K Leszczyński, Katarzyna Niepiekło, Michał Terlecki, Iwona Justyniak, Janusz Lewiński
pmc-11367576.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Redox-active metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are very promising materials due to their potential capabilities for postsynthetic modification aimed at tailoring their application properties. However, the research field related to redox-active MOFs is still relatively underdeveloped, which limits their practical application. We investigated the self-assembly process of Cr(II) ions and isophthalate (m-bdc) linkers, which have been previously demonstrated to yield 0D metal–organic polyhedra. However, using the diffusion-controlled synthetic approach, we demonstrate the selective preparation of a 2D-layered Cr(II)-based MOF material [Cr(m-bdc)]·H2O (1·H2O).

pmc-11475251.title: Complementary Musical Intervention for Patients in Palliative Care in Spain: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-11475251.creator: Inmaculada Valero-Cantero, María Ángeles Vázquez-Sánchez, José Luis Casals-Sánchez, Milagrosa Espinar-Toledo, Juan Corral-Pérez, Cristina Casals
pmc-11475251.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Patients with advanced cancer often endure a heavy burden of symptoms, both in quantity and intensity. Complementary therapies offer potential relief in this challenging scenario. Increasing the number of randomized controlled trials provides a unique opportunity to generate rigorous data, which can be used to establish causal relationships and evaluate interventions; hence, nurses can strengthen evidence-based practices, leading to better patient outcomes and quality of care.

pmc-11550235.title: Preclinical efficacy of oral and nasal rivastigmine-loaded chitosan nano-particles on AlCl3-induced Alzheimer’s-like disease in rats
pmc-11550235.creator: Dina E ElMosbah, Marwa S Khattab, Marwa A Ibrahim, Mona I El-Asssal, Hala M F El Miniawy
pmc-11550235.description: The successful treatment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is still a big challenge. Rivastigmine is one of the most used drugs for the treatment of AD. The short half-life, lower bioavailability, and less concentration of the drug in the brain after oral delivery are considered the main drawbacks of rivastigmine. To improve these drawbacks, nanostructure-mediated drug delivery has gained more attention.

pmc-11635217.title: Protocol of a single-arm, multicenter, phase III trial for selective lymph node dissection in cT1N0M0 invasive non-small cell lung cancer with consolidation-tumor ratio >0.5 located in the apical segment: Eastern Cooperative Thoracic Oncology Projects ECTOP-1018 (SELLAS study)
pmc-11635217.creator: Yiliang Zhang, Chaoqiang Deng, Xiaoyang Luo, Yongfu Yu, Yang Zhang, Haiquan Chen
pmc-11635217.description: BackgroundSystemic lymph node dissection (LND) is the standard procedure for operable invasive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), for radical cure and lymph node (LN) staging. However, its necessity is controversial in early-stage patients without LN metastasis, as evidence shows it could not improve prognosis and may cause surgical complications.

pmc-12523991.title: Influence of Extended Photoperiod Using Blue Light Masks on Hypertrichosis, Coat Condition and General Health Parameters in Horses with Pituitary Pars Intermedia Dysfunction †
pmc-12523991.creator: Sinead Parmantier, Panoraia Kyriazopoulou, Margaret McClendon, Amanda Adams, Barbara A. Murphy
pmc-12523991.description: Simple SummaryThis study involved 52 owner-recruited horses over 15 years old with pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction (PPID), a condition causing excessive hair growth. The horses were divided into two groups. One group (29 horses) wore blue light masks from mid-December to extend their daylight exposure to 15 h daily.

pmc-13286653.title: ZEB1 drives terminal erythroid maturation by controlling the GATA2–KLF1 regulatory switch
pmc-13286653.creator: Alexia Kinoo, Virginie Deleuze, Mohammad Salma, Noémie Legoff, Jérémie Candotti, Pedro Gonzalez-Menendez, Axel Joly, Jérémy Galtier, Julie Charmeaux-Goulot, Sanjay Chahar, Peggy Raynaud, Haoyang Zheng, Betty Rouaisnel, Quentin Bouvier, Céline Faux, Frédérique Verdier, Dominique Helmlinger, Sara El H
pmc-13286653.description: Erythropoiesis is a highly coordinated process governed by lineage-defining transcription factors. While several master regulators have been characterized, many additional factors expressed in erythroid progenitors remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)–associated transcription factor ZEB1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of erythroid maturation.

pmc-13448077.title: Developing UV- protective textiles for workwear applications using various ZnO nanoparticles and cold plasma
pmc-13448077.creator: Nafiseh Nasirzadeh, Farideh Golbabaei, Reza Faridi-Majidi, Mohammad Reza Monazzam Esmaielpour
pmc-13448077.description: Textiles play an important role in workwear by significantly upgrading safety, comfort, and productivity for workers. Recently, new technologies like nanotechnology have played a significant role in the textile industry by providing new functionalities. So, the aim of this study was to develop UV-protective textiles for workwear applications using various ZnO nanoparticles and cold plasma.

pmc-13556824.title: 399. Korean guidelines for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder: strategies for insufficient treatment response and comorbidities
pmc-13556824.creator: H-S Suh, J-H Seo, M-K Kim, C-I Park, Developing committee of Korean guidelines for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder
pmc-13556824.description: BackgroundThe Korean Association of Anxiety Disorders developed Korean guidelines for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) 2024. In this paper, we discussed the consensus among psychiatrists specializing in anxiety disorders, regarding treatment strategies for pharmacological treatment of GAD in Korea.

pmc-13630546.title: Maternal metabolomic signatures for risk of preterm and early term birth in African American women
pmc-13630546.creator: Youran Tan, Donghai Liang, Stephanie M. Eick, Mengyuan Ren, Douglas I. Walker, Xin Hu, Zhenjiang Li, Kaitlin R. Taibl, Elizabeth Corwin, Cherie C. Hill, Dean P. Jones, Anne L. Dunlop
pmc-13630546.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Metabolic signals identifying pregnancies at risk for preterm birth (<37 weeks) and early term birth (37–38 weeks) remain limited. Here we used high-resolution metabolomics to characterize metabolic features associated with spontaneous and medically indicated early birth. We conducted metabolome-wide association studies among 279 (discovery) and 251 (internal validation) pregnant women from the Atlanta African American Maternal-Child Cohort (2014–2018), with serum collected in early (8–14 weeks) and later (24–30 weeks) pregnancy.
